# The `payments:*` CLI

## The MCP surface is one tool, and that is policy

Only `payments_doctor` is exposed. `payments:install` and `payments:configure` mutate the consumer's source tree, and across this ecosystem a mutating command stays off the MCP surface: an agent that can rewrite `lib/config/app.dart` and `lib/main.dart` with no human at the keyboard is a different risk from one that reads a report. Adding either is a policy change, so it does not happen inside a feature branch.

## Install stays manifest-only

The whole install plan fits the v1 `install.yaml` schema (one publish, one provider entry, one config factory), and `InstallCommand` has no fluent override, so there is one place to read what an install does. If a new step cannot be expressed in the manifest, say why in `install.yaml`'s header before writing an override.

## Idempotence comes from the construction, not a guard

A second run converges: the published config rides a transactional write whose content is a pure function of the stub, and the provider and config-factory injections skip when the code is already present. Do not add an "already installed?" early return on top; it hides the case the pre-flight exists to catch.

A file the operator edited by hand is refused because its hash no longer matches the install record. That refusal is the pre-flight working; `--force` is the operator's decision, never a default.

## Command shape

- Declare the command name and its flags in `signature` only. Do not override `name` or `configure(ArgParser)`: `DowelCommand` accepts either form but not both in one command, and every command here uses the signature.
- `configure` and `doctor` declare `CommandBoot.none`, and `install` inherits it from `DowelInstallCommand`. No `payments:*` command is `connected`: none talks to a running app, and one that wanted to would read state the backend already owns.
